notes: The parts list maps the Yún to 'arduino-yun', but that type is not in the visible catalogue, so I defined it as a new part type. Drop the new entry if the catalogue already has it.
The TMP36 is not in the catalogue, so I defined it as 'tmp36' with ports VS, VOUT and GND. Pin order in the image, top to bottom, is +Vs, Vout, GND. This matches the schematic's pins 1, 2 and 3.

The breadboard in the image is rotated. Each horizontal row of 5 holes is one strip, which I mapped to columns 10t, 11t and 12t. The wires go in hole a of each strip. The TMP36 legs go in hole e of each strip.
In the image the red wire goes to the Yún power-header pin just right of 3.3V (the 5V pin). The black wire goes to the first GND pin of the power header (GND.1). The yellow wire goes to A1.
The schematic draws the Vout line going to A0. The circuit image and the text both say A1, so I used A1.
The sketch also uses A0 and A2 as power and ground, but the image does not use them, so the 5V and GND wires are what I built.
The micro-SD card or USB stick, the computer and the network are not part of the wiring, so I left them out.
